summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1a in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/21)

data.turoyo: N. U+čərrə̀k̇ du+dulabo ... dhawxa kosaymi ... ánnaqqa dammər dahino ŭ manduriye du+qayso. ʕAyn xud aṗ+ṗirani d̥komarqi u+laḥmo šk̇ăvá, ánnaqqa u+ketono maḥtíwayle tamo ŭ ʕuzliwa hawxa. U+ketono əzzewa ltamhó ŭ fayšiwa aḥ+ḥabbat harke xud aḥ+ḥəmse kome. Kmo+kìlowat lmore du+ketono ŭ kilo alle, əmṭənwa šawʕo+tmanyo+kìlowat. (07: 57)
data.translation: The roller gin… which they do like so… now then, an oiled iron rod and a wooden roller. Just like these women who flatten unleavened bread, now then, they put the cotton there and they would spin like so. The cotton would go over there and cotton seeds would stay here like black chickpeas. However many kilos for the cotton’s owner and one kilo for them, they brought back seven-eight kilos.

rationale: Single technical subsense 1a attestation: roller apparatus and separation of seeds are essential context.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 1.1/90)

data.turoyo: bəṯr mu nəfoso u ḥa, d huwele əḥtəyaǧ, xaṣṣatan meqəm, ʕuzliwole bi taššiye, saymiwole ḥuṭe bi taššiye bu taʕab dann iḏoṯo, an niše ʕuzliwole.
data.translation: Nach dem Auseinanderzupfen ... wer Bedarf hat ... vor allem früher, da spannen sie (die Wolle) auf der Spindel. In Handarbeit spannen sie sie auf der Spindel zu Fäden – die Frauen spannen sie.

rationale: New Infectum-wa box: wool, spindle, threads and women are explicit; both repeated tokens share one example.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/107)

data.turoyo: Kətwa hawxa tak tuk noše dʕuzliwa medone bu+kušo, əmmíwayle u+kušo.
data.translation: There were people here and there who would spin things by needle; they would call it ‘needle’.

rationale: New Infectum-wa cell: tool bu+kušo, preserving the edition's needle without silently replacing it with spindle.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/27)

data.turoyo: Ánnaqqa gʕuzlíwaynanne bu+dulabo, ʕuzlíwaynanne bu+dulabo hawxa, ŭ saymíwayna u+ʕazlawo kule.
data.translation: Now then, we would spin them with a spinning wheel, we would spin them with a spinning wheel like so, and we would make all that yarn.

rationale: New Infectum-wa cell: suffixed first-person plural and explicit yarn result; both repeated forms share one example.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Farrucke/12)

data.turoyo: Bu+mqamawo məblowa ŭ fəlġowa ʕal ak̇+k̇ačk̇at, ak̇+k̇ačk̇at ʕəzliwa u+ketonayḏa, ǝṯyowa.
data.translation: In that way, she would take it and distribute it among the girls, the girls would spin her cotton, she would come back.

rationale: Fourth new Infectum-wa sense-1 example: explicit cotton object and plural girls.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Famine/55)

data.turoyo: Beǧamat i+naqqayo latwa, ánnaqqa gʕuzlówayne, rafiʕo, rafiʕo, rafiʕo, hawxa saymówayne, hul d̥komalwa.
data.translation: At that time, there were no pajamas, now then I would spin it, thin, thin, thin; so I would do until it would be done.

rationale: Fifth new Infectum-wa sense-1 example: unusual first-person feminine ending -owayne and fine spinning.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (MAC NE Famine/55)

data.turoyo: ‘De k̇ačam, ʕzale, hano rakíxoyo, lo+koxal i+lašayḏan’.
data.translation: ‘Come on, my girl, spin it, this is soft, it it doesn’t not eat our body’.

rationale: New Imperativ box: command to a girl with soft fibre; preserve edition wording.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (115/108)

data.turoyo: u yawmayḏe kule koʕəzlo, i ḥurmaṯe koməfqo ruʕe d qamari bu ʕzolayḏa w ruʕe du qamaryawo, mar koʕayšo ebe yaʕni.
data.translation: Den ganzen Tag spinnt die Frau und verdient mit ihrem Spinnen einen viertel Pfennig, das heißt, von dem viertel Pfennig lebt sie, nimm an.

rationale: New Infinitiv box: possessed action nominal in a self-contained livelihood context.

summary: New sense 1a: Baumwolle am Walzengerät entkernen
rationale: MAC NE Famine/21 describes an iron rod and wooden roller and explicitly says cotton moves onward while seeds remain behind. This is ginning, not yarn formation; one contextual attestation. Whether the verb names turning the roller or the whole operation remains open.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 1.1/92)

data.turoyo: Aʕ ʕeze kqayṣi mənayye marʕeze, u marʕezano kʕuzlile, w məd ʕzəlle, ksaymile baṭṭaniyat, kmaḥtənne ʕal ag gale w kəmʕalqənne m darb as satre, yaʕni kowən lu šufro.
data.translation: Von den Ziegen schert man das Ziegenhaar, das Ziegenhaar spinnt man, und wenn sie es gesponnen haben, stellen sie daraus Kelims her, die sie auf das Bett legen, oder die sie anstatt von Vorhängen aufhängen, d.h. sie dienen der Verschönerung.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: completed spinning as prerequisite within a generic craft sequence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Ishaq Material culture/107)

data.translation: Naturally, I don’t remember when we spun it.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: first-person plural form retained within negated recollection, not asserted personal work.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/92)

data.turoyo: Aʕ ʕeze kqayṣi mənayye marʕeze, u marʕezano kʕuzlile, w məd ʕzəlle, ksaymile baṭṭaniyat, kmaḥtənne ʕal ag gale w kəmʕalqənne m darb as satre, yaʕni kowən lu šufro.
data.translation: Von den Ziegen schert man das Ziegenhaar, das Ziegenhaar spinnt man, und wenn sie es gesponnen haben, stellen sie daraus Kelims her, die sie auf das Bett legen, oder die sie anstatt von Vorhängen aufhängen, d.h. sie dienen der Verschönerung.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: raw goat-hair theme resumed by object suffix; same verse also illustrates the different Preterit box.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Farrucke/9)

data.translation: We’ll spin your cotton, we’ll card it, we’ll spin it’.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: prospective craft promise with full cotton NP and subsequent suffix resumption.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (115/200)

data.turoyo: Koʕəzlo u abrisamano, koməfqole, xəd i manṯo du ṣaʕro, kogəršole. Kəmmət, ʕal u čarx kosaymole.
data.translation: Sie spinnt die Seide so fein wie ein Haar, als ob sie sie auf dem Spinnrad spänne.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: silk as material and the fineness of the thread, without a new sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Farrucke/7)

data.turoyo: Ak̇+k̇ačk̇at, žboyi dməštaʕən ŭ məǧġoli, dəmmənne čirok̇at ŭ guḥxi ŭ ʕuzli u+dolabaṯṯe, šorən i+qəštaṯṯe, ʕuzli u+dolabaṯṯe…
data.translation: The girls, in order to play and chat, to tell stories and laugh and spin their spinning wheel, to card with their bow, to spin their spinning wheel …

rationale: Fifth Infectum example: unusual bare wheel NP beside the ordinary b-instrument; construction noted without a new sense.

summary: Infectum-wa is recurrent across JTM and MAC for customary craft labour; the absent box is now documented with several person/object patterns rather than duplicating every reader's new_form proposal.
Instrument coding includes bi taššiye, bu+dulabo, bu+kušo and ʕal u dulabo. Farrucke/7 has a bare wheel NP; ellipsis or a different argument frame remains possible.
The roller-gin passage differs from actual yarn-spinning at MAC NE Famine/27–28. Only the cotton-seed separation operation gets a technical subsense; turning versus ginning remains to be checked.

The spinning Preterit may occur as a completed prerequisite in generic discourse (JTM 1.1/92) or within negated recollection (MAC Ishaq Material culture/107); neither automatically asserts a specific autobiographical event.
115/103 and 115/108 already appear among the inherited Infectum references and are not added again. PrS 12/6 matches the inherited prs 27/30 context, pending a numbering concordance.
Does ʕuzliwa at MAC NE Famine/21 name ginning as a whole or turning the roller specifically? New technical subsense 1a has one attestation.
Is u+dolabaṯṯe a direct implement object or an instrument without overt b-? No new frame is asserted as settled.
Is kušo a spindle rather than the edition's needle? Confirm gʕuzlówayne as a feminine/dialect ending.
Collate PrS 12/6 with inherited prs 27/30 before correcting references.
Spun material includes wool, goat hair, cotton and silk. Material changes do not establish separate meanings.
